title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: In 2019, the National Confederation of Employers of Moldova (CNPM) implemented a series of actions to assist employers, especially small businesses, in better complying with labour legislation by establishing a new training and advisory service. More concretely, CNPM developed a training curriculum and delivered a series of six trainings across the country reaching out to some 240 enterprises throughout 2019. In parallel, CNPM informed enterprises about incentives available for employment creation, including for workers with disabilities under the active labour market measures foreseen in the new Law on Employment Promotion (nr. 105 of 14/06/2018). In 2020, after the outbreak of the COVID-19 crisis, CNPM moved to digital delivery by conducting three webinars, attended by 96 participants, with focus on various aspects related to the application of labour law in the context of the crisis (telework, dismissals, etc.). The crisis brought into stark relief the fact that CNPM needed to further digitalize the delivery of the new service to be able to enhance its visibility and outreach. Consequently, CNPM developed a concept on how to digitalize its service. Five training modules were developed for an e-learning platform that was launched in October 2021. In addition, CNPM developed a plan on sustainability and promotion (through a more commercial orientation) of the new digital training service. In 2019, the ILO supported the development and implementation of a new labour law training service by CNPM. More specifically, the ILO made external expertise available and advised on the initial concept of the new service. The ILO provided input to the training programme and supported CNPM in delivering a series of trainings to MSMEs across the country. One CNPM staff, competent in the labour law area, contributed to the delivery of trainings, which gave him an excellent opportunity to improve his own knowledge and training skills. In 2021, the ILO provided further support in digitalising the new service. The ILO provided systematic guidance and advice throughout the entire process by revising the content of the training material and of the e-learning platform. CNPM staff was actively involved in the development of training materials and was acquainted with new training methods, which were applied during the interactive webinars that complemented the e-learning platform and were delivered in partnership with labour law experts. The ILO supported CNPM in developing a sustainability and marketing plan that contributed essentially to the uptake of the new service.
